kris: Running into a weird TS/edge problem in the SDK samples. Cloudflare Worker throws ReferenceError: require is not defined. Using the published package in the sample with import.

mike: Make sure the package has an exports map with an import entry. Workers will prefer ESM entrypoints.

kris: Our package.json currently only has main/module/types. No exports map. We did add a dist/worker.mjs but nothing points to it.

ana: For samples we added a small `/edge` subpath earlier: \"exports\": { \"import\": \"./dist/index.mjs\", \"require\": \"./dist/index.cjs\", \"./edge\": \"./dist/worker.mjs\" } and then the sample uses `import {createClient} from 'redwood-sdk/edge'`. That fixed the worker runtime.

lena: Typings question: after changing overloads to a single generic `generate<T = unknown>(opts: GenOpts<T>)`, inference flows but a couple of sample files now show `any` unless users add generics. Is defaulting to `unknown` too painful?

mike: Unknown is the correct safety tradeoff. We should document the ergonomics: show one-liner examples for opt-in typed responses and a pattern using zod for runtime validation. Also add a changelog note.

kris: Build hiccup: esbuild fails with `this` transform when users pass explicit generics in the sample. Stack traces point to `preserveValueImports: true` + `isolatedModules: true` in tsconfig.

ana: For samples we keep a dedicated tsconfig.sample.json: `{"compilerOptions": {"module":"ESNext","target":"ES2020","isolatedModules":true,"declaration":false,"preserveValueImports":false}}`. That keeps esbuild happy and avoids eliding imports that are side-effectful.

ci-bot: ci: sample-edge (node 18) build failed earlier, logs posted: https://ci/edge/77777

mike: Action items: 1) add exports map + `/edge` subpath, 2) switch SDK overloads -> single generic with discriminant union, 3) add tsconfig.sample.json + short README snippet about esbuild flags, 4) update changelog about unknown default. I'll pick the typings change, @kris pls handle sample packaging.

kris: Will open PR with two commits (packaging + typings) and tag reviewers. Thanks all!
